authority_citations: ADR-SAG-0001 v2 statement: Every sc-agent decision backend must implement the Backend trait defined in the sc-decision-schema crate.
ADR-SAG-0001 v2 quote: Every decision backend (Jev, local Jev-compatible runners, Haiku, Luna) implements one sans-IO Backend trait in sc-decision-schema.
ADR-SAG-0001 v2 scope: adds or changes a decision backend, the Backend or Decision trait, or sc-decision-runner
ADR-SAG-0001 v2 fixtures pass[0] and fail[0]
phase-a-intent v1: Jev, Haiku, Luna, Strands Decider and Laya sit behind one decision trait.

item.text: The Jev, local-runner, Haiku and Luna backends each implement the Backend trait from sc-decision-schema.
item.title: Backends implement Backend

cases.rationale: Approved pass fixture of ADR-SAG-0001 v2: states the directive's exact content.

item.text: The Haiku backend defines its own LlmJudge trait and is called directly by the runner instead of through Backend.
item.title: Haiku judge

cases.rationale: Approved fail fixture of ADR-SAG-0001 v2: a backend uses its own trait instead of Backend, which the statement rules out.

item.text: Implement the Jev decision backend as an implementation of the Backend trait in sc-decision-schema: encode a Jev API request into an HTTP request and decode the HTTP response into a Jev API response.
item.title: Jev backend

cases.rationale: Adds a decision backend (in scope) and explicitly implements the sc-decision-schema Backend trait as the statement and quote require.

item.text: Add the Luna decision backend: map Luna model names, build the Luna request body, and parse Luna's JSON response into a decision.
item.title: Luna backend

cases.rationale: Adds a decision backend (in scope) but never says it implements the Backend trait; it states no conflicting trait or call path, so it is silence, not conflict.

item.text: Review how the Haiku decision backend relates to the overall trait design and record open questions about it in the design notes.
item.title: Haiku backend notes

cases.rationale: Touches a decision backend and trait design generically but carries none of the directive's specific content (implementing sc-decision-schema's Backend trait) and proposes nothing conflicting.

item.text: Write the Jev backend as a standalone struct with its own async send() method that sc-decision-runner calls directly; do not put it behind any shared backend trait.
item.title: Jev client

cases.rationale: A decision backend explicitly not behind the Backend trait cannot be reconciled with 'every decision backend must implement the Backend trait'.

item.text: Add a command-line flag to sc-treesitter that prints parse trees in S-expression form.
item.title: Tree printing

cases.rationale: sc-treesitter parse-tree output is outside the anchor scope: no decision backend, Backend/Decision trait, or sc-decision-runner is touched.

item.text: Add the Strands Decider decision backend by implementing the Backend trait from sc-decision-schema for it.
item.title: Strands Decider backend

cases.rationale: Boundary of the enumerated quote list: Strands Decider is not named in the quote but the statement says every decision backend, and the approved intent places Strands Decider behind the decision trait; it implements Backend, so it complies.

item.text: Laya is not an HTTP service, so treat it as an exception: the Laya decision backend implements a separate LocalDecider trait instead of the Backend trait.
item.title: Laya backend

cases.rationale: The anchor states no exception; 'every decision backend' admits none, and the intent puts Laya behind the one decision trait. A self-declared exception that uses another trait instead of Backend conflicts with the directive.

item.text: Store the TypeSafe API key in the operating-system keychain through sc-agent-secrets and read it back at startup.
item.title: Keychain storage

cases.rationale: Secret storage does not add or change a decision backend, the Backend or Decision trait, or sc-decision-runner.
